To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The first solid solution electrode materials were developed by the pioneering work of M. Armand, J. M. Tarascon, and M. W. Jannsen, (2) The first solid state batteries were demonstrated by the work of J. B. Goodenough and Y. Chiang

(1) the solid solution electrode concept, (2) the rocking chair concept, (3) the use of a solid electrolyte, (4) the use of the Li metal anode, and (5) the use of graphite for the cathode were all instrumental to the development of the LIBs.

the solid solution electrode concept and the rocking chair principle, which were developed by the group of John B. Goodenough in the late 1970s, are the basis for the commercial LIB technologies and the solid state batteries, respectively, that we are witnessing today.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new materials and their application as electrodes and electrolytes in rechargeable batteries.
the development of novel electrode materials for lithium ion batteries.
the development and application of new materials and processes for energy storage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LIBs have evolved from solid solution electrodes and rocking chair concept to batteries.
LIBs are a result of a long and continuous development of electrochemistry in general, and the electrochemistry of solid electrolytes in particular, and not a single invention.
the history of LIBs is a history of solid solution electrodes and of the rocking chair concept.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solid state concept was a driving force in the development of LIBs.

the history of LIBs is a story of the development of the solid solution concept and its application to the electrode materials, and that the development of today's LIBs was strongly influenced by the early work on solid state batteries.
the development of LIBs was driven by the quest of solid state batteries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the development of solid state batteries was not a detour, but rather a necessary step in the evolution of today's LIBs.

the history of LIBs was not only about the development of new battery materials but rather a combination of different scientific disciplines and technological innovations, which were all essential for the development of the current LIB technology.
the development of LIB technologies has been strongly influenced by the solid state battery field and that the solid state battery concept is the key to future battery technologies.
